**motion-launch-videos 2.0** turns one kinetic-type skill into eight styles of launch video, each its own skill in the same plugin, on a shared core.

**Install or update (inside Claude Code)**
```
/plugin marketplace add Kimeur/motion-launch-videos
/plugin install motion-launch-videos@motion-launch-videos
```
Then ask, for example: *"Make a 12 second launch video for https://your-product.com, cartoon style"*

**Eight styles**
| Skill | Makes |
|---|---|
| `motion-launch-videos` | kinetic-typography bumpers and identity stings |
| `motion-shapes` | flat 2D motion graphics: icons that draw on, pop and ripple, wipes, animated SVG logos |
| `motion-cartoon` | an original mascot on twos with a boiling line: hops, walks, waves, speech bubbles, a sign |
| `motion-3d` | extruded, bevelled type and logos, primitives, soft shadows, an orbit camera (WebGL2, no libraries) |
| `motion-charts` | counters, bars, lines and donuts bound to sourced data; the critique fails dishonest charts |
| `motion-pixel` | pixel art in a strict palette: sprites, parallax, tile maps, a bitmap font |
| `motion-particles` | thousands of particles that form words and marks, burst and reform |
| `motion-ui` | your app's screens in a device frame: taps, scrolls, pushes, toasts, callouts |

Each has its own engine, automated critique, docs and a rendered example in [`examples/`](https://github.com/Kimeur/motion-launch-videos/tree/main/examples).

**Also new**
- **Cycle loops:** a film can keep moving through the loop point (a spinning ring, a mascot's breath, a scrolling world), and `loopcheck` requires the seam to be as smooth as any other instant.
- **A shared core** for springs, loops, motion blur, type layout and the critique, kept in step across every skill by `tools/sync.mjs`; `tools/check.mjs --smoke` builds and checks every demo.
- **Fixes that reach every skill, the kinetic one included:** text is antialiased in grey without the red and blue fringes headless Chromium drew on an opaque canvas; `fonts.mjs` fetches several weights of one family; `--gif-colors N` gives N colours.

**Requirements:** Node 20+, ffmpeg with libx264, a Chromium (`render.mjs doctor` checks everything). The 3D style uses WebGL2: the GPU when there is one, a software renderer when there is not (slower).



Full changes: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Kimeur/motion-launch-videos/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
